_how: Text and game settings per mission. Safe to edit without coding: change the words, add facts or news links. game.rule: sign -1 = only 'got darker' counts, 1 = only 'got brighter', 0 = both; db = how strong the change must be; water_max = after must be darker than this dB (99 = off). game.focus = [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions of the picture (optional): only change inside counts. camera: {clouds: 'yes'|'no'} asks in step 1 whether a normal camera could see the ground that day (NASA GIBS photo); false hides the photo layer. layers: which map layers start switched on (towns, roads, rivers). bonus: a list of questions asked after the game, answers worked out from the radar + OpenStreetMap: {type: town|river|area|share, question, explain, of (share: change|land|wet)}; see js/games/bonus.js. camera.layer 'hls' = the sharp Landsat/Sentinel-2 photo (needs a clear date). say: {glow, find} replace the guide's text in steps 2 and 3. game.glow: 'plain' shows every change instead of greying what doesn't count. why: replaces the 'Why?' line on the score screen. offer: extra layers this mission may show in 🗺 Layers (wet_before, wet_after); the wet layers appear nowhere else. tutorial: true makes this the training mission (js/tutorial.js): it comes first, opens by itself for new players, and the alien explains every step.

W1.story: In October 2026 a storm called DANA Adam poured rain on the coast near Gandia, Spain, and fields and streets filled with water.
facts: The storm hit eastern Spain on 17–19 October 2026.
More than 1,000 people were rescued and about 2,000 were evacuated.
Near Gandia, homes by the beach were flooded.

news.title: Four deaths reported as DANA Adam flooding prompts more than 1,000 rescues in eastern Spain
4 dead as severe floods hit eastern Spain, thousands evacuated

bonus.question: 🚁 Rescue time! Which town is right next to the biggest flood?
bonus.explain: {town} is only {km} km from the biggest flood. Rescue teams use radar flood maps like yours to know where to send boats, even when it's cloudy.

bonus.question: 🌊 Which river is right next to the biggest flood?
bonus.explain: {river} runs only {km} km from it. In a storm, rivers and gullies fill up fast and spill over into fields and streets.
That's the kind of number rescue teams and insurance need after a flood.

W2.story: In January 2026 weeks of heavy rain made the Limpopo River in Mozambique burst its banks and flood the valley around Chokwe.
facts: NASA used NISAR to compare the open water on 5 and 17 January 2026.
Rain in December and January filled the rivers until they overflowed into towns and fields.
Radar sees the flood even under thick rain clouds.

news.title: NISAR Reveals Major Flooding in Mozambique

camera.note: January is the rainy season in Mozambique.

bonus.question: 🌊 Which river burst its banks?
bonus.explain: {river} is only {km} km from the biggest flood. After weeks of rain it spilled over into the fields around it.

bonus.question: 🚁 Rescue time! Which town is closest to the biggest flood?
bonus.explain: {town} is only {km} km from the biggest flood. Radar flood maps like yours show rescuers where the water is, even under clouds.
And that's only inside this picture: the whole flood was even bigger.

D1.story: Along the BR-163 highway in the Amazon rainforest, people cut down forest in the dry season of 2026.
facts: About 6,000 trucks drive the BR-163 every day.
Forest disappears fastest right next to roads.
Brazil tracks new clearing with satellites every few days.
Road map: © OpenStreetMap contributors.

news.title: Crackdown lets rainforest reclaim illegal road in rare win for the Amazon
Deforestation surges in Xingu, one of Amazon's most important basins

camera.note: Over the rainforest there are clouds almost every day, so radar is super useful there.

bonus.question: How much forest was cut, all together? The yellow square is 1 km × 1 km.
bonus.explain: All of that was rainforest in June.

bonus.question: What part of this whole picture is new clearing?
bonus.explain: My radar measured {pct} % of the picture, cut in just four months.

D3.story: A giant nickel mine in Weda Bay, Indonesia, clears rainforest to dig up metal used in electric-car batteries.
facts: Weda Bay is the world's biggest nickel mine.
At least 5,331 hectares of forest were cleared for nickel mining on Halmahera island.
In 2025 Indonesia took back part of the site for cutting forest without permission.

news.title: Foreign-backed nickel hub in Indonesia causing mass deforestation – report
Indonesia seizes part of nickel site over forest violations
Photos: The lives and forests bound to Indonesia's nickel dreams

A1.story: In Punjab, India, farmers flood their rice fields in June, the rice grows tall, and it is harvested in autumn.
facts: After the harvest some farmers burn the leftover straw, which makes the air smoky as far as Delhi.
By 4 November 2026 Punjab counted 2,347 straw fires.
Burnt rice fields fell from 14.6 % in 2025 to 7.9 % in 2026.

news.title: In Punjab and Haryana, tech is curbing stubble burning, but battle is far from over

frames.clue: Planting time: farmers flood the rice paddies. Water is smooth, so the fields look DARK.
Growing time: the rice is tall and leafy. Plants send lots of echo back, so it looks BRIGHT.
Harvest time: the rice is cut, only short straw is left. In between: medium and patchy.

bonus.question: What part of these farms changed a lot between June and November?
bonus.explain: My radar measured {pct} %. Almost all of Punjab's farmland is rice in the summer, so the whole picture changes with the seasons.

bonus.question: Which village is right next to the biggest change?
bonus.explain: {town} is only {km} km from it. Its farmers flooded, grew and harvested rice there.

A3.story: Training mission: in the Jezreel Valley in Israel, summer crops grew in June and were harvested by October. Learn how radar sees it, step by step.
facts: The Jezreel Valley is called the breadbasket of Israel.
Farmers grow wheat, cotton, sunflowers, corn, chickpeas and watermelons.
Summer crops need drip irrigation because the summer is dry.

news.title: Jezreel Valley: The Breadbasket of Israel

camera.note: This sharp photo is from the Sentinel-2 satellite, one day before my radar pass. Summer in Israel is almost always sunny.

bonus.question: 🚜 Which village is right next to the biggest harvested field?
bonus.explain: {town} is only {km} km from it. Farmers there harvested their summer crop between June and October.

bonus.question: How much farmland was harvested, all together? The yellow square is 1 km × 1 km.
bonus.explain: Radar can count harvests for a whole country, even at night.

L3.story: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is shrinking. Where water dries up, the lakebed is left bare, and the wind blows its dust into the cities. Find the newly dried lakebed!
facts: The white lines (🗺 Layers → 💧 Wet) show where my radar saw water or wet mud in June: smooth and wet looks dark to radar.
Blue-green inside the lines means it got brighter by October: the mud dried and cracked, so it's rougher.
The lake ended 2025 at its third-lowest level since 1903.
When the lakebed dries out, wind blows its dust into nearby cities.
On 8 July 2026 a dust storm made the air four times dirtier than the healthy limit.

news.title: Great Salt Lake ends 2025 at its third-lowest level
Researchers say they're getting closer to answers on Great Salt Lake dust

bonus.question: 💨 Dust alert! Which town is closest to the biggest new dry patch?
bonus.explain: {town} is only {km} km from it. When strong wind blows over dry lakebed, the dust can reach towns like this one.

bonus.question: How much new dry lakebed glows, all together? The yellow square is 1 km × 1 km.
bonus.explain: Every bit of new dry lakebed is a place where wind can pick up dust.

say.glow: It glows! The WHITE lines show where it was WET (dark) in June. BLUE-GREEN inside them = it got brighter = it dried out: new dry lakebed! Grey = it doesn't count.
say.find: Inside the white lines it was wet in June. Find the {n} big BLUE-GREEN patches there: lakebed that dried out! Tap right on them!

M3.story: Barataria Bay in the Mississippi River Delta has oil and gas platforms standing in the water. Metal makes a super-bright radar echo, like a tiny star on the dark water. Can you find them all?
facts: Platforms stand on the sea floor, so they're in the same place in every radar picture. Ships come and go.
On 29 November 2025 NISAR saw the delta clearly while clouds hid it from normal cameras.
Louisiana loses coastal wetlands every year to rising seas and sinking land: the marsh islands you see are shrinking.
Wetlands protect cities like New Orleans from storm waves.

news.title: NASA-ISRO radar mission peers through clouds to see Mississippi River Delta
Satellites help scientists track dramatic wetlands loss in Louisiana

M3.why: Metal ships and platforms have corners that bounce my radar straight back, like a mirror ball, so they shine super bright on the dark, smooth water.

bonus.question: 🌿 How much of this picture is still marsh and land, not open water?
bonus.explain: My radar measured {pct} % land; the rest is open water. Louisiana loses about a football pitch of wetland every 100 minutes, so the water keeps growing.
